[b]Administrator House on Military Inspection[/b]

In the rapid expansion of the New Vegas Defense Authority, Administrator House has went on a campaign to show citizens how the extra funding and the NVDA expansion plan is working on bolstering the great warriors of New Vegas. House has first gone to inspect the Army, which showed its vast fleet of APCs, ready to be used at any moment. The Air Force was next where the fleet of J-10s flew over head in a show of confidence. The Navy was last where the submarines were toured by House, the ships took him on a small patrol to show their effective guarding of New Vegas waters.

New Vegas has, with confidence, finally got a military worthy of protecting it!

[i]The Amaryllis Times - Der Amaryllis Zette. Friday, February 25th 2028[/i]

President William Manor has been sworn into duty, in a great ceremony in Amaryllis. Hundreds of thousands appeared for the ceremony, with President Manor meeting his supporters and speaking to the people.

In his inaugural speech, Manor spoke of change and hope, bringing focus on reforms. Together, we will bring newfound prosperity and reform to our Union, striking back at the divisions that plague us. It is a time of hope, it is a time of change, said the new President, appealing to the time of President Rayne, before he went on to start his day at Government House.

[quote=yzakastan;61466443][b]The Arrival[/b]
Word would spread quickly to the Shah that the Wuloosyans had sent their new foreign minister Eikelboom, appointed following her predecessor stepping aside due to the war in Rosenmarkke. 
The shah, not really in the mood to meet with the Wuloosyans at the moment, requested that someone with Great vigor go meet the delegation on the tarmac. The Yzak State Department would approve Cahit Alparslan to meet with the delegation as the representative for the Yzakastanian Shah, along with the foreign minister Izık Öldur. 
The Wuloosyan jet would be permitted to land at the Vyzmír International Presidential Airport, its sleek sides shining in the warm and humid early spring sunlight. Cahit would be seated in his wheelchair, a gold-topped cane clutched in his hand, resting lazily against his leg, a fez perched precariously atop his head. Beside him stood the fifty-year-old Izık Öldur, adjusting his tie as aides walked themselves into place. [/quote]
